source1: Trenton Barnes, 'Teotihuacan', Heilbrunn Timeline of Art History, Metropolitan Museum of Art, 2024 - https://www.metmuseum.org/toah/hd/teot/hd_teot.htm
source2: Mark Cartwright, 'Teotihuacan', World History Encyclopedia, 2015 (non-academic; gives internal uprising or Xochicalco) - https://www.worldhistory.org/Teotihuacan/
notes: Civic core along Street of the Dead burned c. 550 CE by unidentified persons; burning targeted elite/state buildings, widely read as internal uprising, but outsiders not excluded; population fell below 30,000 after 600. Database end 649 late.

successor: Monte Alban Late I (Monte Alban-centred Zapotec polity)
source1: UNESCO World Heritage Centre, 'Historic Centre of Oaxaca and Archaeological Site of Monte Alban' (Zapotec capital flourished 500 BC to AD 850) - https://whc.unesco.org/en/list/415/
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Monte Alban' (successive continuous phases of Monte Alban culture) - https://www.britannica.com/place/Monte-Alban
notes: Early/Late I is a ceramic-phase split; Monte Alban, founded c. 500 BCE as Zapotec capital, kept growing through Late I and II with no break in the central place. Britannica's earlier founding date differs.

source2: Encyclopaedia Iranica, 'Abbasid Caliphate' (Turkish amir al-umara dominance; Buyid 'Daylami intermezzo' eclipsing caliphs) - https://www.iranicaonline.org/articles/abbasid-caliphate
notes: Daylamite Buyid army of Ahmad b. Buya, based in Fars/Jibal, entered Baghdad 19 Dec 945 without a fight after the amir al-umara regime collapsed; caliphs kept only religious authority. Prior Turkish commanders' strife (Q4).

Manethonian dynastic break only: Hetepsekhemwy ('peaceful in respect of the two powers') became first 2nd-dynasty king and moved royal burials to Saqqara; kingship continued. Name may hint at earlier strife (Q4 U).

Late Woodland I/II is a typological subdivision of the same local Late Woodland tradition in the American Bottom; no central authority, no evidence of a break. Coded by inference only; no source could be retrieved.

Geometric/Archaic is a pottery-style boundary c. 700 BCE; Crete comprised many independent poleis (Knossos, Gortyn etc.) with no island-wide authority, and settlements continued into the Archaic period. Inference only; no source retrieved.

successor: Kingdom of Spain under Joseph Bonaparte (French Napoleonic client); Bourbons restored 1814
source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Ferdinand VII' (imprisoned in France by Napoleon 1808-13; king again 1814) - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Ferdinand-VII
notes: French troops held Madrid 1808; Napoleon forced Bourbon abdications at Bayonne, made Joseph king (1808-13); Ferdinand VII captive in France until 1814 restoration. Database end 1814 marks restoration, but Bourbon authority broke 1808. Aranjuez mutiny 1808 = Q4.

source1: Thomas E. Emerson and Kristin M. Hedman, 'The Dangers of Diversity: The Consolidation and Dissolution of Cahokia', in Beyond Collapse, SIU Press, 2015, pp. 147-178 - https://experts.illinois.edu/en/publications/the-dangers-of-diversity-the-consolidation-and-dissolution-of-cah
notes: c. 1050 'Big Bang' rebuilt Cahokia as a planned centre; isotope data suggest up to one-third of residents were immigrants, so the local population persisted (not replacement); no conquest documented.

source2: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Puyi' (forced to abdicate 12 Feb 1912, ending 267-year Qing rule) - https://www.britannica.com/biography/Puyi
notes: 1911 Revolution (10 Oct 1911 to 12 Feb 1912), a domestic nationalist revolt, forced Puyi's abdication, ending Qing rule and the imperial system and creating a republic. Boxer crisis and repeated revolts preceded it (Q4).

source1: Encyclopaedia Britannica, 'Shunga dynasty' (rule ended about 73 BCE) - https://www.britannica.com/topic/Shunga-dynasty
